title: HEaring impairment After Radiotherapy in patients with OroPharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
summary:
This study focuses on patients who have been diagnosed with a tumour in the larynx or throat. A common treatment for this is radiotherapy. Hearing is crucial to quality of life, and in order to minimise the impact of treatment as much as possible, it is important to investigate the long-term effects of radiotherapy in detail. One possible adverse effect of radiotherapy in this area is hearing loss. As few large-scale studies have yet been conducted on humans in this regard, we wish to investigate this potential hearing loss in our patients and determine the effects of the radiation dose. 

The study focuses on gathering information about your hearing and how your hearing ability may change as a result of potential radiotherapy. To this end, we are comparing patients who receive radiotherapy as part of their standard treatment with patients who do not receive radiotherapy. In addition, patients receiving radiotherapy will be randomly divided into two groups. One group will receive standard radiotherapy, whilst the other group will receive an adjusted radiation regimen.  All groups will undergo the same hearing tests as part of this study. This will enable us to improve future radiotherapy treatments and prevent hearing loss without reducing the effectiveness of the treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Diagnosis of oropharyngeal carcinoma (OPSCC) 
-Radiotherapy as part of the treatment 
-Adequate hearing function prior to the start of treatment
Exclusion criteria:
-Pre-existing severe hearing loss
-Previous radiotherapy to the head and neck region
-Concomitant medical conditions or medications that 
affect hearing
-Patients are unable to participate in audiological procedures
